title: Switching and Ethernet
summary: Connect switch ports, Ethernet links, and interface status to network behavior.
objectives: Explain the role of a switch and its ports.
Interpret link state and uplink evidence.
Distinguish a physical connection from a complete logical path.

vocab.def: A switch or device connection point for a network link.
A family of standards and technologies used for wired local networking.
An indication that an interface detects an active or inactive connection.

sections.heading: Switches forward traffic
sections.body: A switch connects devices on a local network and forwards traffic using information about interfaces and addresses. A link light or status value is evidence of connection, not proof that every service works.

sections.heading: Document the physical layer
sections.body: Port labels, cable IDs, and uplink notes help another person reproduce the path. Use synthetic records and never change a production switch.

practice.prompt: A server port is up but its switch uplink is down. What can you conclude?
practice.answer: The server has a local link, but the path beyond that switch may be unavailable; inspect and document the uplink evidence.

quiz.question: What is a safe interpretation of an active Ethernet link?
options: The interface detects a physical connection
The cable is connected to the correct destination
quiz.answer: The interface detects a physical connection

lab.objective: Interpret synthetic switch-port and Ethernet link records.

futureCompetencyCandidates: interpret switch and Ethernet link evidence
reflectionPrompt: What evidence would you need beyond link state before declaring a network path healthy?
